story_title: How Netomi Scales Enterprise AI Agents with OpenAI Architecture
caption:
How do you scale autonomous AI agents without risking enterprise operations? 🤖⚙️

Netomi handles millions of customer interactions using OpenAI models—not by relying on simple prompts, but by building a multi-step concurrent governance framework.

Swipe through for the breakdown of how enterprise AI agents actually scale in production.

alt_text_overall: GetByteRush carousel explaining how Netomi scales enterprise AI agents using multi-step reasoning, concurrency, and real-time governance layers.
alt_text_per_slide: Slide 1: HOW AI AGENTS ACTUALLY SCALE. Netomi automates millions of enterprise customer interactions. Here is how they built multi-step AI agents that do not fail in production. — shown as a side-by-side comparison.

Slide 2: THE SINGLE-PROMPT LIMIT. Standard LLM implementations attempt to solve complex multi-step tasks in one shot. In enterprise workflows, a single hallucination destroys system trust. — shown as one large highlighted number or word.

Slide 3: CONCURRENCY + REASONING. Netomi orchestrates multi-step workflows by pairing advanced OpenAI models with concurrent execution pathways, validating actions before execution. — shown as pinned reference facts.

Slide 4: ZERO UNCHECKED ACTIONS. Every automated action passes real-time policy checks. If confidence scores fall below threshold, the agent seamlessly routes the task to human teams. — shown as a side-by-side comparison.
Slide 5: PREDICTABILITY OVER SPEED. In enterprise agentic systems, deterministic system guardrails around LLMs matter more than raw speed or speculative intelligence. — shown as a pulled quote.

Slide 6: THE NEW AI STACK. Building production AI isn't just about prompt engineering. It requires building robust traditional software wrappers to govern probabilistic models. — shown as a side-by-side comparison.

Slide 7: AGENTS ARE SOFTWARE SYSTEMS. The future of enterprise AI isn't standalone autonomous models. It is disciplined software architecture giving models precise operational boundaries. — shown as a closing statement with the GetByteRush signature.
